deities: Lord Mahavira (24th Jain Tirthankara) - white, 4-ft idol in lotus posture, famed as the 'moustached Mahavira'
festivals: Annual fair on the 13th day of Chaitra (Chaitra Shukla Trayodashi)

history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Svetambara Jain temple, keep-or-drop decision needed. One of the Gorwad Panch Tirth (with Ranakpur, Narlai, Nadol, Varkana). The white idol of Mahavira is celebrated for a legendary moustache: Rana Raj Singh I of Mewar, finding a white hair while applying saffron, demanded to see the moustache; after the priest's three-day fast, the deity revealed a moustache, and when the Rana uprooted it, milk (or blood, per variants) oozed out - hence 'Muchhala (moustached) Mahavir'. Nagara-style curvilinear shikhara, intricately carved torana, two large black elephant idols at the entrance; managed by the Anandji Kalyanji Trust. Inside Kumbhalgarh Sanctuary, ~5 km from Ghanerao; dharamshala and bhojnalaya on site. CSV town 'Pali' imprecise - actual village is Ghanerao, Desuri tehsil.

name: Muchhal Mahavir Temple
town: Ghanerao, Desuri tehsil (CSV town 'Pali' is imprecise - temple is ~5 km from Ghanerao village, not Pali city)
town_description: Ghanerao is a heritage village cradled among Aravalli peaks in Desuri tehsil of Pali district, on the Falna-Kumbhalgarh route. Known for its garasia-tribal villages, wildlife setting inside the Kumbhalgarh Sanctuary, and a cluster of old Jain temples that make it a Jain tirth hub near Ranakpur.

travel.railway: Falna railway station - about 40 km (25 miles).
travel.road: About 5 km from Ghanerao inside Kumbhalgarh Sanctuary; reachable by bus/taxi from Falna.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Chaitra (March-April) for the annual fair on the 13th day.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify - confirm locally); dharamshala and bhojnalaya available on premises.
